correctness.rationale: For equiprobable multinomial counts, conditional K=k is uniform over k!S(N,k) surjections, independently of which k cells are chosen. Pearson X²=m−N+(2m/N)U where U counts equal-cell unordered pairs. Contracting one pair gives S(N−1,k), contracting any two distinct pairs (overlapping or disjoint) gives S(N−2,k). These determine E U=Ma and Var U=M a(1−a)+M(M−1)(b−a²), M=binom(N,2), hence both exact displayed moment formulas for every m,N≥2, 1≤k≤min(m,N). Independent rational enumeration of every labeled allocation sequence (hence exact multinomial weights) for m=2..5,N=2..6 covered 60 feasible (m,N,k) strata and matched both moments. Finite tests corroborate, but uniform proof is surjection contraction.

value.rationale: Conditional finite-sample mean and variance of Pearson goodness-of-fit conditional on number of sampling zeros are natural sparse-table calibration quantities. Both moments are closed Stirling-ratio formulas for every feasible (m,N,k), not a rebranding of an unconditional moment or a tiny slice; a researcher can use them for occupancy-stratified diagnostics. No claim for unequal probabilities.
